description: Release-blocker checklist for the first production deployment of MicroRhodoDB website 2.0 (dataset v1.6.0). Read by web/scripts/release_gate.py. A blocker is resolved only when status is 'resolved' with a valid maintainer resolution record (decided_by = GitHub login, decided_at = YYYY-MM-DD not in the future, reference = https URL on a non-reserved host; no placeholders) AND its automated check passes. The 12 blockers in this file are mandatory: removing one, re-scoping it away from 'production', duplicating it or using a status other than 'open'/'resolved' blocks production. Production mode requires --online and the full 40-character --sha (exit 2 otherwise). Only the maintainer may change status; the gate and the deployment tooling never do. Blockers stop production deployment only; local development, tests and preview builds are not blocked.

resolution_template.reference: URL of the issue, PR or commit recording the decision

resolution.notes: Data, documentation and release artifacts: CC BY 4.0. Source code (src/, pipeline/, workflow/, tools/, web/, tests/): MIT. LICENSE states both and includes the MIT text; README.md, web/package.json, CITATION.cff and .zenodo.json agree.

blockers.title: Data/code licence statements are inconsistent
blockers.evidence: LICENSE: CC BY 4.0 for database content, documentation and release artifacts, and source code under src/, pipeline/, workflow/, tools/ 'released under the same terms'. README.md: 'Data: CC BY 4.0. Code: MIT.' Website manifest/footer (from README): 'CC BY 4.0 (data); MIT (code)'. CITATION.cff and .zenodo.json: CC-BY-4.0. web/package.json: MIT.
blockers.required_decision: Maintainer chooses the code licence (and whether web/ is covered) and updates LICENSE / README.md / web/package.json consistently. Legal choice; not made by the tooling.

resolution.notes: Authoritative v1.6.0 release date 2026-10-10 (GitHub Release published 2026-10-10T10:16:26Z, CHANGELOG.md, release notes, .zenodo.json). CITATION.cff corrected from 2026-10-09.

resolution.notes: No DOI has been minted for v1.6.0 and none is claimed. CITATION.cff (message and url), README.md and the website Citation page direct users to cite the release version and the GitHub Release. A DOI may be added in a later release.

blockers.title: No DOI and no approved alternative citation policy

blockers.required_decision: Maintainer fills every <<PLACEHOLDER>> in MAINTENANCE.md with a truthful statement ("no dedicated funding" and "no named successor" are acceptable if true).

resolution.notes: BINARIES.md corrected (907d472): the prior-release databases are documented as not on the Release, and only Release assets use path | bytes | sha256 rows. A newly created archive, MicroRhodoDB_v1.6.0_only.tar.gz (11,984,255 B, SHA-256 d093ba26b72b512dbbc8550931a3763951fc3706a8a9f7ce49fffe5737f9fb14), and its .sha256 were uploaded to Release v1.6.0 and listed in BINARIES.md (1e257b5). It is derived from the original deposit archive with releases/v1.0, v1.3.0, v1.4.0 and v1.5.0 removed, documented in PACKAGE_NOTES.md inside it; the original MicroRhodoDB_v1.6.0.tar.gz was not re-created. Check verified 2026-10-24: Release has all 3 listed assets with matching sizes.

blockers.title: GitHub Release v1.6.0 lacks assets that BINARIES.md says are attached
blockers.evidence: GitHub API (docs/website/pr6a/evidence/github_releases.json): Release v1.6.0 has one asset, microrhododb_v1.6.0.sqlite (33,464,320 B, SHA-256 matches). BINARIES.md also lists microrhododb_v1.5.0.sqlite, microrhododb_v1.5.0_env_pilot.sqlite, microrhododb_v1.4.0.sqlite, microrhododb_v1.3.0.sqlite, microrhododb_v1.0.sqlite and MicroRhodoDB_v1.6.0.tar.gz with its .sha256 'attached to the same Release'. Local copies of the five historical databases exist and match the BINARIES.md SHA-256 values; no copy of the tar.gz exists and no checksum for it is recorded anywhere.
blockers.required_decision: Maintainer either uploads the missing assets (the five databases from verified local copies; an archive only if one can be produced and documented truthfully as a newly created file) or corrects BINARIES.md to describe what the Release actually contains. Never fabricate or re-create historical binaries under their original names without verification.

resolution.notes: No archival (Zenodo) deposit exists. The deposit claims were removed from MAINTENANCE.md (BINARIES.md already made none); .zenodo.json is kept only as metadata for a possible future deposit.

blockers.title: Zenodo deposit is claimed but unverified
blockers.evidence: BINARIES.md: databases 'deposited on Zenodo'; MAINTENANCE.md: 'Zenodo (DOI <<PLACEHOLDER>>)'; .zenodo.json exists; no DOI is recorded and no deposit could be verified.
blockers.required_decision: Maintainer confirms the deposit and records its DOI, or removes the deposit claim until it exists.

The switch is a repository setting that only the maintainer may change, immediately before an authorised deployment (see PR7_DEPLOYMENT_RUNBOOK.md).

blockers.title: github-pages environment allows PR branches and has no required reviewers
blockers.evidence: docs/website/pr6a/evidence/github_environments.json and github_pages_branch_policies.json (queried 2026-10-11T20:19:32Z): protection rules = [branch_policy] only (no required reviewers); custom deployment-branch policies = 'None' (a policy literally named None), 'main', 'website/pr-1-exporter', 'website/pr-3-protein-entry'; can_admins_bypass = true.
blockers.required_decision: Maintainer restricts deployment branches to main and adds a required reviewer (Settings > Environments > github-pages). Automated check (online): a required_reviewers rule with at least one reviewer, custom branch policies only, exactly one policy named 'main' of type 'branch'. Enabling 'Prevent self-review' and disallowing admin bypass are recommended; the gate reports both but does not enforce them (maintainer decision).

blockers.required_decision: Push the branches, open the PR, and record a successful web-data run (and a site-preview run) on the exact commit to be deployed. The deploy workflow re-checks this online.
